cards.name: CMYK conversion for press
cards.summary: RGB artwork and photos are converted to the printer's CMYK profile once, at the end, with out-of-gamut colours tamed first, so the press result matches the approved proof.
use_for: brochures, posters and packaging that started in RGB
avoid: screen, web or social output: stay in RGB
converting back and forth: every conversion loses colour; keep an RGB master and convert a copy
brand colours with official CMYK builds: type the official values instead of trusting a conversion
converting before the printer names a profile: ask first (coated, uncoated and newsprint profiles differ a lot)

steps.note: Edit > Color Settings: CMYK working space = the printer's profile, or a regional Prepress preset (app.colorSettings = '<settings name>').
Select > Color Range > Out Of Gamut (with View > Proof Setup set to that profile) to select the colours that will clip.

Masked by that selection: lower saturation a little so clipped colours fall back into gamut smoothly. Photoshop adjustment step: not render-verified yet (the Photoshop adjustment gallery is still being built), so its confidence is capped at medium.

Edit > Convert to Profile: destination = the printer's CMYK profile, Intent Relative Colorimetric + Black Point Compensation (Perceptual for very saturated photos). DOM: doc.convertProfile(profile, Intent.RELATIVECOLORIMETRIC, true, false). Run it on a copy: the verified event flattened a layered document.
File > Document Color Mode > CMYK Color (the only scripted switch; id paired by alignment, not confirmed by execution). Better: start the document in CMYK.
Edit > Edit Colors > Convert to CMYK on the selected art (confirmed); check spot and global swatches afterwards.
Tools > Color Management: default CMYK profile = the printer's; Preserve pure black and Map gray to CMYK black on (Application.ColorManager.PreservePureBlack / MapGrayToCMYKBlack for scripts).
A ready prepress colour-settings preset (ISO Coated v2 CMYK); use the North America Prepress one for SWOP-style presses.
Bitmaps > Mode > CMYK Color (32-bit) on each placed photo.
Vector colours: Color.ConvertToCMYK() on each fill / outline colour; Color.IsInGamut flags colours the press cannot reach (unverified).

manual_steps: Soft-proof before and after (see the soft proof recipe); the Gamut Warning view in Photoshop cannot be scripted.
cards.note: Photoshop adjustment step: not render-verified yet (the Photoshop adjustment gallery is still being built), so its confidence is capped at medium.

cards.name: Rich black vs 100K black
cards.summary: Large solid black areas print as a rich black build (for example C60 M40 Y40 K100) while body text, thin rules and barcodes stay pure 100K so they cannot misregister into coloured fringes.
use_for: black backgrounds and big black display type
posters and covers with large dark areas
keeping small type and barcodes crisp
avoid: rich black on small text, hairlines or barcodes: four plates must register exactly; use 100K
the 400 % registration black (C100 M100 Y100 K100): it never dries and smears; use the printer's build
exceeding the printer's total ink limit (often about 300 % on coated, lower on uncoated): ask for it
Photoshop photos: their black is already built by the CMYK conversion (GCR / UCR); do not repaint it

steps.note: Two global swatches: text and lines c0 m0 y0 k100; large areas and display type over about 24 pt c60 m40 y40 k100 (240 % total ink) or the printer's own build (doc.swatches.add(), swatch.color = new CMYKColor()).
Edit > Edit Colors > Overprint Black: Add Black, 100 %, Fill and Stroke, so the 100K text overprints instead of knocking out (dialog; DOM: fillOverprint / strokeOverprint = true).
Preferences > Appearance of Black: display and output all blacks accurately, so the screen shows the difference between 100K and rich black.
Use the palette's K100 swatch for text and lines, never its last 400 % swatch.
Rich black for large areas: Color.CMYKAssign(60, 40, 40, 100) (or the printer's build); keep a named colour style for each black.
Separations: AlwaysOverprintBlack = True so 100K objects overprint at output (unverified).

manual_steps: Check the black plates in Illustrator's Separations Preview (no script route) or CorelDRAW's Print Preview with separations on.

cards.name: Overprint black text and keylines
cards.summary: Black text, thin black keylines and trap strokes are set to overprint, so slight plate misregistration cannot open white gaps, and the result is checked in an overprint preview.
use_for: thin black outlines around coloured shapes
avoid: white or light objects: overprinting makes them disappear on press
coloured (non-black) objects over other colours: the inks mix into a new colour; preview first
RGB / screen work: overprint only matters in CMYK or spot separations
Photoshop: pixel layers have no overprint attribute; set it in the vector layout

steps.id: internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-attributes
steps.note: Attributes panel: Overprint Fill / Overprint Stroke on the selected black objects. DOM: pathItem.fillOverprint = true, strokeOverprint = true; type: textRange.characterAttributes.overprintFill = true (unverified).
View > Overprint Preview to see the inks mix as on press.
Object > Overprint Fill on the selected black text and shapes (Shape.OverprintFill = True).
Object > Overprint Outline on black keylines (Shape.OverprintOutline = True).
View > Simulate Overprints (ActiveWindow.ActiveView.SimulateOverprints = True) to check.

manual_steps: Final check of the plates: Illustrator Separations Preview (by hand) or the printer's proof.
built_from: internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-attributes

cards.name: Bleed and crop marks
cards.summary: Background art runs 3 mm (0.125 in) past the trim on every side, and the press PDF carries the bleed and crop marks.
avoid: important text or logos inside the bleed or close to the trim: keep a 3-5 mm safe zone
marks drawn inside the artboard: they get trimmed or printed; let the PDF export add them
screen-only output: bleed does not apply

steps.note: Image > Canvas Size, Relative: +6 mm width and height (3 mm a side), anchor centre, then extend the background art into the new strip; executeAction 'canvasSize' (verified live).

Crop marks for a Photoshop-only job: File > Print > Printing Marks (Corner Crop Marks); for a press PDF place the image in Illustrator or CorelDRAW and add marks there (Photoshop's PDFSaveOptions has no marks members).
File > Document Setup: Bleed 3 mm (8.504 pt) on all four sides (scripts can set bleed only at creation, through a DocumentPreset).
o.pDFPreset first, then o.trimMarks = true; o.bleedOffsetRect = [8.504, 8.504, 8.504, 8.504] (pt); doc.saveAs(file, o).
Only to mark one item on a larger artboard (a card on a sheet): apply it to a plain rectangle of the trim size (verified).
Bleed is a page / document setting: set ActiveDocument.Unit first, then the Bleed property (0.125 in / 3 mm) (unverified).
View > Page > Bleed shows the bleed line: pull the background past it.
PDFSettings.IncludeBleed = True, Bleed (typelib unit 'tens of micron': check on a test export), CropMarks = True.
File > Publish to PDF (ActiveDocument.PublishToPDF(path)).

cards.name: Outline text for hand-off
cards.summary: Live type is converted to vector outlines (curves, shapes) in a copy of the file that goes to print, so missing or unembeddable fonts cannot reflow or substitute.
use_for: logos and display type sent to printers, sign makers and cutters
files opened on machines without the fonts
avoid: the working master: outlines cannot be turned back into text; keep a live-type copy
long body copy: it bloats the file; embed the fonts in a PDF/X instead
type that still needs corrections: finish the copy first

steps.note: On a saved copy: select the type (doc.textFrames) and Type > Create Outlines; DOM textFrame.createOutline() (id paired by its shortcut, not confirmed).
On a copy: Object > Convert to Curves on the text (confirmed by the harvest); or at export time PDFSettings.TextAsCurves = True.
Type > Convert to Shape: the type layer becomes a vector shape layer that stays sharp in a Photoshop PDF (verified live); duplicate and hide the type layer first.

cards.name: Flatten transparency for press
cards.summary: Opacity, blend modes, soft shadows and glows are flattened into opaque pieces at press resolution for workflows that cannot take live transparency (PDF/X-1a, older RIPs).
use_for: spot-colour jobs with shadows or glows
avoid: the master file: flattening is destructive; keep transparency live and flatten a copy or at export
PDF/X-4 workflows: they keep live transparency, so nothing needs flattening
low flattener settings near text and thin lines: they rasterize or thicken; outline the text
judging CorelDRAW bitmap effects on a half-size preview: they lose pixel-scale detail; check at 1:1

steps.note: Raster effects (shadows, glows, Photoshop Effects) render at 300 ppi before anything is flattened (verified setting).
Flattener Preview with [High Resolution]: highlight Rasterized Complex Regions and All Affected Objects.
On a copy: preset [High Resolution], Convert All Text to Outlines; or keep the file live and let the PDF/X-1a export flatten (PDFSaveOptions.flattenerPreset).
The flattener preset for final press output (name only harvested).
Bakes layer styles into pixels first.
On a duplicate (Image > Duplicate): Layer > Flatten Image (verified live: one Background layer; transparent areas fill with white).
On a copy: s.FlattenEffects() bakes live bitmap effects into one bitmap (needs_input card, not render-tested).
Objects with drop shadows or transparency over spot colours: Convert to Bitmap, CMYK, 300 dpi (Shape.ConvertToBitmapEx; its default is only 72 dpi).
Then publish with pdfVersion = pdfVersionPDFX1a.

cards.name: PDF/X press export
cards.summary: The press PDF is written to a PDF/X standard: PDF/X-4 when the printer takes live transparency, PDF/X-1a when it wants everything flattened CMYK or spot.
avoid: web or email PDFs: use a smallest-file-size preset
keeping Illustrator editing data in a press PDF: it makes big files anyone can reopen
PDF/X from an RGB Photoshop file without a destination profile and output condition: the save fails or falls back

steps.note: o.pDFPreset = '[PDF/X-4:2008]' (exact name, brackets included) before any override; use '[PDF/X-1a:2001]' for flattened CMYK.
o.preserveEditability = false; o.trimMarks / o.bleedOffsetRect as needed; doc.saveAs(file, o). saveAs re-targets the open document: save the .ai master first.
o.PDFStandard = PDFStandardType.PDFX42008 (or PDFX1A2001); o.preserveEditing = false; o.layers = false; doc.saveAs(file, o, true) on a CMYK document (or set destinationProfile and outputCondition).
ActiveDocument.PDFSettings: Reset, pdfVersion = pdfVersionPDFX4 (or pdfVersionPDFX1a), IncludeBleed, CropMarks, EmbedFonts; then ActiveDocument.PublishToPDF(path).
Dialog route: File > Publish to PDF with a PDF/X preset; read the Issues tab before saving.

cards.name: Soft proof on screen
cards.summary: The design is viewed on screen through the press profile (soft proof), with out-of-gamut colours flagged and single plates inspected, before any conversion or hard proof.
use_for: checking RGB art before CMYK conversion
spotting colours that will dull on press
showing a client roughly how the print will look
avoid: an uncalibrated monitor: the proof misleads; calibrate or ask for a hard proof
treating it as a contract proof: it is a preview only
leaving proofing on while picking colours for screen output

steps.note: View > Proof Setup > Working CMYK (or Custom for the printer's own profile).
View > Proof Colors toggles the soft proof.
View > Gamut Warning greys the colours the press cannot reach (no confirmed script route).
Optional: Proof Setup > Working Cyan Plate (and the other plates) to inspect single separations.
View > Proof Setup > Document CMYK.
View > Proof Colors.
View > Overprint Preview, so overprints and spot inks show as they will mix.
Color Proofing docker: pick the output profile and turn on the gamut warning.
View > Proof Colors (ActiveView.ShowProofColors = True).
View > Simulate Overprints.

cards.name: Spot colours on their own plates
cards.summary: Brand or special inks are defined as named spot colours from a colour book so they separate onto their own plates, and the plates are checked before output.
use_for: brand colours that must match exactly
metallic, fluorescent, white ink or varnish plates
avoid: process-only (CMYK) digital jobs: convert spots to process or they may print wrong
the wrong colour book for the stock: pick the coated / uncoated set that matches the paper
judging a spot ink on screen: the swatch shows an approximation; use a printed ink guide
the same ink defined twice under different names: it separates onto two plates

steps.note: Window > Swatch Libraries > Color Books: add the ink from the book that matches the stock (HKS N here, uncoated) to Swatches.
Scripted: var sp = doc.spots.add(); sp.name = '<ink name>'; sp.colorType = ColorModel.SPOT; sp.color = <alternate>; item.fillColor = new SpotColor() with .spot = sp, .tint = 100 (unverified).
Pick the ink from the spot palette (locked palette, one plate per swatch).
Keep spots on export: OutputSpotColorsAs (not the hidden SpotColors member).
Spot, white-ink or varnish plate: var c = doc.channels.add(); c.kind = ChannelType.SPOTCOLOR; c.name, c.color, c.opacity (unverified); save as Photoshop PDF with spotColors = true.

manual_steps: Check every plate: Illustrator Separations Preview (by hand), CorelDRAW Print Preview with separations.

cards.name: Minimum line and type sizes
cards.summary: Strokes, rules and small type are checked against press minimums: no hairlines (lines 0.25 pt / 0.1 mm or more), body type 6 pt or larger, reversed or four-colour small type larger and bolder.
use_for: fine print, legal lines and labels
avoid: CorelDRAW's Hairline Outline in print art: it can vanish on press; set a real width
thin serif type reversed out of a dark four-colour background: the ink fills in; use a heavier weight or a single ink
Photoshop raster art: line and type sizes are set in the vector layout

steps.note: Select a hairline sample, Select > Same > Stroke Weight; scripted: loop doc.pathItems and flag strokeWidth under 0.25 pt.
Raise flagged strokes: pathItem.strokeWidth = 0.25 (or the printer's minimum).
Flag textRange.characterAttributes.size under 6 pt, and reversed or four-colour type under about 8 pt.
Replace Shape.Outline.Width values under 0.25 pt (document units: set ActiveDocument.Unit first).
Then read the Issues tab of Publish to PDF; its colour-mode checks are off in this default style, switch them on or load the printer's style.

cards.name: Image resolution for print
cards.summary: Every photo and raster effect is checked for at least 300 ppi at its final printed size (150-200 ppi is usually enough for large posters seen from a distance) before the PDF is made.
use_for: raster effects (shadows, glows) in vector files
avoid: upsampling a 72 ppi web image and calling it print-ready: detail is not added; source a larger image or use an AI upscale and check it
judging CorelDRAW bitmap effects on a half-size preview: they lose pixel-scale detail; check at 1:1
resampling when only the print size changes: turn Resample off

steps.note: Image > Image Size with Resample off: set Resolution 300 and read the print size (or set the size and read the ppi); resample (Preserve Details 2.0) only when the ppi is short.
View > Print Size to judge the image at roughly its physical size.
Links panel > Link Info: each placed image's PPI after scaling (aim for 300).
Document Raster Effects Settings at 300 ppi, so raster effects are not rendered at screen resolution (verified setting).
File > Document Properties lists every bitmap with its colour mode: a quick inventory.
Bitmaps > Resample on bitmaps under the target (Bitmap.Resample, unverified).

cards.name: Package fonts and links
cards.summary: The job is collected with its fonts and linked images, or links are embedded, so the print shop can open and output it without missing files.
use_for: sending native files to a printer or another designer
avoid: cloud-only fonts that are not copied by packaging: outline them or have the recipient activate them
packaging when the printer only wants a PDF: send the PDF/X
embedding huge linked files you still update elsewhere: the link to the source is cut

steps.note: Links panel: fix missing or modified links first.
File > Package: Copy Links, Copy Fonts, Create Report (dialog; the document must be saved).
Layer > Smart Objects > Embed All Linked (verified live), so the PSD carries its linked files.
Or File > Package to copy the PSD plus a Links folder (no confirmed script route; it was disabled in every harvest state).
File > Document Properties: check the font and bitmap inventory.
Deliver a PDF with EmbedFonts = True (or TextAsCurves) via PublishToPDF; PGD has no card for a collect-for-output command.
